artists.biography: Jonathan Wilson (born December 30, 1974, in Forest City, North Carolina) is an American singer/songwriter/multi-instrumentalist/producer who is now based in Los Angeles.  Wilson completed a solo album entitled, Frankie Ray in 2007 that was never officially released. Since then, Wilson has recorded the full length album, Gentle Spirit, which was released in 2011. The same year, Wilson was named Uncut Magazine's 2011 "New Artist of the Year".   Wilson's early experiences was as co-founder pf the band muscadine with Benji Hughes in 1995. The band released their debut album, The Ballad of Hope Nicholls, in 1998.  Wilson's recording studio, Five Star Studio, in Echo Park, Los Angeles, is renowned for its sound and analog recording equipment.  www.songsofjonathanwilson.com

perplexity.description:
Jonathan Wilson’s Rare Birds, released on March 2, 2018 via Bella Union, is the third studio album from the Los Angeles-based singer-songwriter and producer. The album blends elements of rock, folk, and electronic music, reflecting Wilson’s signature style rooted in the Laurel Canyon mellow rock tradition while incorporating modern textures and psychedelic flourishes. Self-produced at his Five Star Studios, Rare Birds features lush arrangements, introspective songwriting, and guest appearances from notable artists such as Lana Del Rey, Father John Misty, and Laraaji, adding depth and variety to its expansive sound.

Musically, Rare Birds stands out in Wilson’s discography for its ambitious scope and genre-blurring approach, merging vintage California rock with subtle electronic experimentation and world music influences. The album’s 78-minute runtime allows for a rich, immersive listening experience, marked by atmospheric production and melodic sophistication. Critics responded positively, with outlets like The Line of Best Fit awarding it 8/10 and several publications including it in their year-end lists. While not a mainstream commercial breakthrough, Rare Birds solidified Wilson’s reputation as a thoughtful, genre-defying artist within the indie and alternative rock scenes.
